newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Nov 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Nov 1.

text.p: Boeing Co's next generation of 747 jumbo jets might cost $7 billion to build, 40 percent more than the last estimate, the Wall Street Journal reported on Friday.
- Archer Daniels Midland Co named three executives to share the responsibilities of Dwayne Andreas, who will nevertheless remain chairman and chief executive officer.
- General Motors Corp and the United Automobile Workers are arguing over whether the company should have the right to reduce its hourly work force.
- Justice Clarence Thomas declined a request by federal regulators to reinstate rules to open the local telephone market to competition.
- Carrington Laboratories Inc said clinical tests of a product for treating ulcerative colitis had no therapeutic effect.
- Pharmacia & Upjohn Inc posted a 12-percent fall in quarterly profit.
- Apple Computer Inc cut the prices of its Power Macintosh computers by 9 percent to 30 percent.
- Car makers are offering cash rebates on their 1997 models in an effort to keep a strong U.S. light vehicle market.
- The Securities and Exchange Commission is trying to find out if mutual funds have been getting rebates from brokerage firms that execute their trades.
- An Alabama state court judge ordered the disclosure that General Motors Corp has paid $67 million to settle a number of lawsuits over an allegedly faulty door latch.
- Personal income rose 0.6 percent in September but consumer spending edged 0.1 percent higher.
- Crude oil prices are staying around six-year highs but stock and bond investors have yet to see inflation rise.
- Stocks and bonds rallied following the release of jobs data.
- Amid signs that the U.S. economy is slowing down, investors are taking profits on fashion and luxury good companies like Tiffany & Co Inc, Gucci Group NV and Saks Holdings Inc.
- The bond market rallied and pushed the yield on the bellwether 30-year bond to the lowest level in almost seven months.
